title: Pocket Field Guide to Staying Alive
author: Ray Kowalski
pages: Rule one: water first. A person can go three weeks without food but only three days without water. Know where your water is before you know where your bed is.
Rule two: fire is a tool, not a toy. Keep it small, keep it covered, and put it out before you sleep. A fire you can see from a mile away will be seen from a mile away.
Rule three: wood is everything. Logs make planks, planks make sticks, and a good furnace turns a log into charcoal that burns as hot as coal. Never waste a log.
Rule four: high ground, one way in. Pick a place you can defend. A door you can barricade is worth more than a big house you can't.
Rule five: keep a sharp blade. A good machete clears brush, cuts rope, and keeps you alive when everything else fails. Treat it well and it will treat you well.
